Container.Name: fwupd-webui
Container.Overview:
Firmware inventory and updates for your server. Lists every device fwupd can see — NVMe drives, SATA disks, HBAs, network cards, Thunderbolt controllers, docks — with its current firmware version and any updates available from LVFS.
Read-only by default. Firmware flashing is off unless you set FWUPD_WEBUI_ENABLE_FLASHING to true; while it is off, the flash routes do not exist at all. Even when enabled, every flash requires typing the device name to confirm, storage devices carry a data-loss warning, and system firmware (BIOS, UEFI capsule, SPI flash) is refused outright.
Requires privileged mode. Enumerating firmware means issuing NVMe admin commands and SCSI ioctls, which an unprivileged container cannot do — without it you will see only the CPU and display.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: fwupd firmware lvfs bios nvme ssd hba thunderbolt update
Container.Requires: Privileged mode and host access to /sys, /dev and /run/udev. Internet access for LVFS metadata.
Container.Changes:
### 0.1.1 Show the application version in the UI header and in /api/status.
### 0.1.0 First release. Firmware inventory with optional flashing, off by default.

Config.Name: sysfs
Config.Description: Required: fwupd reads device attributes from sysfs

Config.Name: devices
Config.Description: Required: NVMe and SCSI ioctls need the host device nodes

Config.Name: udev database
Config.Description: fwupd's udev database. Harmless to leave enabled.

Config.Name: Metadata cache
Config.Description: Persists downloaded LVFS metadata across restarts

Config.Name: Metadata refresh interval (hours)
Config.Description: How old LVFS metadata may be before startup refetches it

Config.Name: Enable flashing
Config.Description: Set to true to allow writing firmware to devices. Leave false for a read-only inventory. Enabling this permits irreversible writes to hardware. Every flash requires typing the device name to confirm, and storage devices show a data-loss warning. Stop the array before flashing any array drive.

Config.Name: Flash timeout (seconds)
Config.Description: Hard timeout for a single firmware write
